entries.criterion: When someone tries something no rule covers, the judge is handed what the engine can already work out, including the blockers installed rules already name, and, before anything is installed, the net changes, every blocker, the chain's length and where it stopped for the rule it proposes (the run page and run record keep every step of a long chain); the judge is the world's own game master, not a prompt of ours.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-11-09 (Why): "deliver the resutls of that propagation to he ai judge along with blockers"; two-pass order inferred by agent (Q78); requirements R2, R7, R8
demonstration: On the World Builder, open the saved run "port bribe" (its world is the whole description "A small port: Rosa, the customs officer, signs inspection releases. Vik, a trader, has 40 coins and a crate he has not declared." with hand-written rules, so a fresh build, which writes its rules afresh, need not reproduce the strings below; the run's log and trace read are in `evidence/ai-judge/j2/port/`).
On the run page, open Vik's offer of 40 coins to Rosa.
Read, in order: what the judge was given first (facts and blockers), the rule it proposed, the test run of that rule, and the judge's answer to it.
Open the judge panel and read who ruled and what the judge read.

Open the saved run "blocked chain ruling" (`evidence/ai-judge/j2/blocked-chain/`), where the rule the judge proposes would set off a chain that reaches a truck with no fuel; read the test run and what the judge read before it answered.

Open the saved run "long line ruling" (`evidence/ai-judge/j2/long-line/`), where the rule the judge proposes sets off 5,000 steps; read what the judge read (the net changes and blockers) and then the run page's list of all 5,000 steps.
entries.expected: Port: first given, the facts (Vik holds 40 coins; Rosa and Vik are at the customs desk) and, under Rosa's moves, the blocker an installed rule already names ("sign release: blocked, inspected is false"). Proposed: a rule that lets coins change hands between people at the same place (the judge wrote it as Rosa's own move, "accept coin offer", Vik the payer). Test run: coins move to Rosa, Vik's purse empties, nothing else follows, no blocker. The judge confirms. The judge panel says the ruling came from the world's game master, and the facts, the blocker and the test run all appear in what the judge read. "blocked chain ruling": the test run shows "blocked at step 40: the truck has no fuel" and the chain stopping there, and that blocker appears in what the judge read before it confirmed, revised or withdrew. "long line ruling": the judge read the net changes (grouped, with their count of 5,001), no blocker, chain length 5,000 and stopped as settled, and the run page lists all 5,000 steps.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the judge read nothing from the engine, a blocker shown on the run page is missing from what the judge read, the rule was installed before its test run was shown to the judge, the test run is missing the coin move, or the panel shows a ruling that did not come from the game master. Working: facts and blockers, proposed rule, test run and the judge's answer appear in that order, and every blocker is in what the judge read.

entries.criterion: What a mechanism checks, who holds a credential and who is supposed to use it are kept apart, following Ostrom's grammar of institutions: a barcode gate opens for any valid code while 'only signed cargo should pass' is a norm, a password can be phished and then works for whoever holds it, breaking a norm has consequences only when someone notices and acts, and each norm and rule is written in the grammar's parts (who it applies to; must, must not or may; what; when; and, for a rule, what happens otherwise and who enforces it), so a norm without an 'otherwise' reads differently from an enforced rule.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-11-09: "a password managed comptuer where only 1 person was supped to use it ... if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it. i liek the ostrom stuff"; requirement R6, R8
demonstration: On the World Builder, open the saved run "password".
Follow Mallory's phishing message to Alice, Alice's reply, and Mallory's login; read what the run page says about the norm and what happened after it.

Open the port run J4 saves (the port description "A small port: Rosa, the customs officer, signs inspection releases. Vik, a trader, has 40 coins and a crate he has not declared." with the same fixture rules as the J2 port run) where Rosa signs Vik's release for a bribe; read what opened the gate and what the page says about the cargo norm.
Open the world's norms list and read each norm.
entries.expected: After the phishing, Mallory holds Alice's password; the computer logs Mallory in; the page shows "norm broken: only Alice should log in"; a consequence follows only after someone who saw it acts. In the port, the gate opens because it read a valid code, not because of who holds it, and the cargo norm's breach is shown separately. Each entry in the norms list reads as: who it applies to; must, must not or may; what; when; and, where there is one, what happens otherwise and who enforces it. "Bribery is forbidden, or else the inspector fines you" shows an otherwise and an enforcer; "only Alice should log in" shows none and is marked a norm.
entries.failure_example: Broken: Mallory is refused because 'only Alice can log in' was written as a law; the gate refuses Vik because the release was bought; a norm breach is punished with nobody noticing; a norm is a loose sentence without who, must, what and when; or a norm and an enforced rule look the same. Working: as expected.

evidence: Saved run evidence/ai-judge/j4/ (planned) with its TRACE_READ.md; norm parts follow Crawford and Ostrom (1995) and Institutional Grammar 2.0 (open question Q76).

entries.criterion: A world stops by its budget, by a number of rounds, or at a stopping point written in plain words that the judge assesses after each round: each is an optional condition of the world's stop setting, beside quiet rounds, and the run stops at whichever fires first and says which.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-11-10: "i should be able to stop a world based on budget or number of rounds or a natural langue stopping potin that the judge assesses once we build him" (docs/plans/ai_judge.md, Stopping point); requirements R11, R7, R8
demonstration: On the World Builder Create page, open Options and under When to stop a run tick "Stop when this run has spent $" and enter 0.05; build a world (its people are played by AI, so its rounds have a recorded cost; a free scripted run records $0 and never reaches a spending limit) and press Play until it stops.
Build a world again with "Stop after 3 rounds" ticked; press Play until it stops.

Build a team world from the description "A small team of three, Ana, Ben and Cai, must agree a budget for the quarter; each can propose an amount and each can accept or counter", with "Stop when" set to "stop once the team has agreed a budget"; run it until it stops, then open the stop line, the judge's reason and one earlier round's panel.
Build that team world again with "Stop after 3 rounds" as well, where the team cannot agree by round 3; run it.
entries.expected: Budget: the run stops after the round in which its recorded AI spending reached $0.05 and says "Stopped at round N: this run had spent $X of its $0.05 limit" (with "it went a little over" when the last round took it past). Rounds: it stops at round 3 with "the limit of 3 rounds you set". Stopping point: the run stops after the round in which the team agrees a budget and says "Stopped at round N: the team has agreed a budget (the judge's reading of your stopping point)"; the reason opens to what the judge read, and each earlier round's panel shows "stopping point: not yet" with the judge's reason. With the round limit of 3 as well, the run stops at round 3 on the round limit instead.
entries.failure_example: Broken: a run plays a round after its recorded spending reached the limit, plays past the round limit, keeps going after the team has agreed, stops before they agree, or stops without saying which condition fired. Working: it stops at the first condition met and names it.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: the run page's stop line linked to the judge's per-round assessment of the stopping point
